question: Does the OECD/COINr density pipeline (definition filtering × recipe sampling × normalization by elements_with_bbox) preserve the task-type discrimination of sample-derived features (tag_entropy, form_fraction, total_area) when these features are used as element-level weights replacing the hierarchy-weighted density formula, or does the pipeline structurally collapse between-type variance regardless of input feature?
hypothesis: The hierarchy-weighted density formula's eta2=0.0 (normalized form) was caused by the specific inForm binary weighting combined with normalization collapsing between-type variance. Feature-weighted densities using tag_entropy, form_fraction, or total_area as element weights should preserve discrimination (eta2 >= 0.05) through the full OECD/COINr pipeline because these features capture genuine structural differences between page types that survive definition filtering and normalization. The sample's within-type template invariance guarantees eta2=1.0 for raw feature values; the pipeline test is whether definition-based element subsetting and elements_with_bbox normalization change the relative ranking of page types or destroy the discriminative signal.
falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if ANY of: (F1) ALL feature-weighted density eta2 values through the pipeline are < 0.05 on page_type across all 3 definitions × 3 features (the pipeline collapses all feature-based discrimination); (F2) The pipeline reorders page types such that the ranking of mean density values contradicts the direct-feature ranking for ALL features simultaneously (the pipeline inverts the discriminative signal); (F3) Normalized feature-weighted density produces eta2=0.0 for at least one feature that achieves eta2=1.0 as a direct value AND the normalized hierarchy density also produces eta2=0.0, indicating the pipeline normalizes away ALL between-type variance regardless of input.

baselines.description: Direct feature eta2=1.0 on page_type: tag_entropy (listing 2.646 vs detail 2.484 vs cart 2.602), form_fraction (0.85 vs 0.95 vs 0.95), total_area (341k vs 589k vs 428k). Within-type std=0.0 for all. Established in EXP-INTEL-35409927864 M2 (audit PASS) and replicated in EXP-INTEL-35422991016 M2-M4.
baselines.source: EXP-INTEL-35409927864 result.json M2, EXP-INTEL-35422991016 result.json M2-M4

baselines.description: Parent hierarchy-weighted density eta2=0.0 on page_type with normalized formula (EXP-INTEL-35401997918 M7). The exp(-alpha*depth) with binary inForm depth produces identical normalized density across page types when inForm distribution is task-invariant. C1 anchor from compute_output.json shows raw binary inForm sum gives eta2=1.0 (unnormalized), confirming normalization is the collapse mechanism.

Recipe choice produces 31x canonical/weighted density gap (EXP-INTEL-35264637598). Linear combinations cannot break OECD/COINr dominance degeneracy (EXP-INTEL-35353016702). Within each recipe definitions are highly correlated Spearman r > 0.98 (EXP-INTEL-3330747199).

positive_control.description: Direct (non-pipeline) computation of tag_entropy, form_fraction, and total_area eta2 on page_type reproduces eta2=1.0 with the same group means and within-type std=0.0 as parent EXP-INTEL-35409927864 M2. This confirms the raw features retain discrimination on the frozen sample before any pipeline processing.
positive_control.expected: All three features: eta2=1.0, within-type std=0.0, listing_mean/detail_mean/cart_mean within 0.001 of parent values

null_control.description: The normalized hierarchy-weighted density formula (sum(exp(-alpha*depth)*inForm) / total_weight) produces eta2 < 0.01 on page_type, reproducing the parent's eta2=0.0 anchor (EXP-INTEL-35401997918 M7). This confirms the normalization collapse is reproducible and establishes the C1 anchor that the parent experiment failed to produce in its own artifact.
null_control.expected: Normalized hierarchy density: eta2 < 0.01, all page type means within 1% of each other

measurement_validity: All computations use existing raw evidence from EXP-INTEL-34782350557 (sha256: da30bd059adb555409784a2fd41402d53b64a25c89aa710b77e686a94a155050). No new data collection required.
The 7 tasks (3 listing, 3 detail, 1 cart deduplicated) with truncated-first-20 locatable_sample are the input. Within-type template invariance is inherited (EXP-INTEL-35409927864 M1).

OECD/COINr definitions use the SAME role mappings as prior experiments: DEF-FULL-MAP (a→link, input→textbox), DEF-FORM-ONLY (form roles only), ISOLATED-A-LINK (link only, no menuitem/tab). Code from EXP-INTEL-35083033552 analyze.py.

Feature-weighted density = sum(feature_value(elem) for elem matching definition) / elements_with_bbox. This replaces the element COUNT with a feature VALUE sum while preserving the definition filtering and normalization structure.

The hierarchy formula normalization uses: normalized_density = raw_hierarchy_sum / total_hierarchy_weight where total_hierarchy_weight = sum(exp(-alpha*depth) for all 20 elements). Alpha=0.3 from parent (EXP-INTEL-35401997918).
Metrics bounded to 7 tasks, 1 Magento site, 3 definitions, 2 recipes, 3 features. Cart n=1 within-type variance degenerate; comparison focuses on listing vs detail.
No browser/network/model calls. Fully offline computation on reconstructed data.
decision_rule:
Conjunctive:

C1_RAW_FEATURES_REPRODUCE: The positive control PC1 passes: all three direct features achieve eta2 >= 0.99 on page_type with within-type std < 0.001. PASS if all three pass; FAIL if any eta2 < 0.99.

C2_HIERARCHY_NORMALIZED_REPRODUCES: The null control NC1 passes: normalized hierarchy density eta2 < 0.01 on page_type. PASS if eta2 < 0.01; FAIL if eta2 >= 0.01.

C3_FEATURE_PIPELINE_ETA2_NONZERO: At least one feature-weighted density through the OECD/COINr pipeline (any definition × any recipe × any feature) achieves eta2 >= 0.05 on page_type. PASS if max(eta2) >= 0.05; FAIL if all eta2 < 0.05.

C4_PIPELINE_PRESERVES_RANKING: For at least one feature, the OECD/COINr pipeline (across all 3 definitions × 2 recipes) preserves the same ranking of page types as the direct feature (listing > detail for tag_entropy, detail > listing for form_fraction and total_area). PASS if >= 1 feature preserves ranking across all 6 definition×recipe combinations; FAIL if all features have at least one definition×recipe that reverses the listing-vs-detail ordering.

C5_FEATURE_BEATS_HIERARCHY: The best feature-weighted pipeline eta2 is strictly greater than the normalized hierarchy density eta2 (which should be ~0.0 from C2). PASS if max_feature_eta2 > hierarchy_eta2 + 0.01; FAIL otherwise.

VERDICT RULES:
- If NOT C1: MEASUREMENT_INVALID — raw features don't reproduce, cannot anchor.
- If NOT C2: MEASUREMENT_INVALID — hierarchy anchor fails, cannot compare.
- If C1 AND C2 AND NOT C3: FALSIFIES — pipeline collapses ALL feature-based discrimination. The OECD/COINr framework structure (definitions × recipes × normalization) destroys between-type variance regardless of input feature. Density-based MIXED handling is not viable through this pipeline.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND NOT C4: MIXED — some features survive the pipeline with eta2 >= 0.05, but the pipeline reverses the natural ranking. Feature-weighted density is achievable but produces different task-type ordering than raw features. Product must decide which ordering is correct.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND C4 AND NOT C5: MIXED — pipeline preserves discrimination and ranking, but feature-weighted density is no better than hierarchy density. The hierarchy formula was not the bottleneck.
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND C4 AND C5: SURVIVES — feature-weighted density achieves non-zero discrimination through the OECD/COINr pipeline, preserves ranking, and beats the hierarchy formula. The hierarchy formula was the bottleneck, not the pipeline. Product can pursue density-based MIXED handling using feature-weighted density.
product_consequence_positive: Resolves the MIXED program bottleneck: feature-weighted density through OECD/COINr pipeline achieves task-type discrimination. The hierarchy formula (not the pipeline) was the bottleneck. Product lane can pursue density-based MIXED handling using tag_entropy-weighted or total_area-weighted density with the existing definition×recipe framework. The 31x recipe material gap (EXP-INTEL-35264637598) becomes actionable with feature-weighted density as the input metric.
product_consequence_negative: If the pipeline collapses all feature-based discrimination (C3 fails), the OECD/COINr framework structure itself is the bottleneck, not the specific formula. Density-based MIXED handling should be abandoned for this sample/site. Product lane must pivot to non-density-based approaches or await per-task sampling from the runtime lane.
estimated_cost: VERY LOW — offline computation on existing reconstructed data. No browser/network work. Compute feature-weighted density for 3 features × 3 definitions × 7 tasks = 63 feature-weighted sums, plus 3 definitions × 2 recipes × 7 tasks = 42 recipe-sampled densities, plus eta2 for 9 feature×definition combinations. Estimated < 3000 LLM tokens.
expected_information_gain: HIGH — directly tests the critical untested question from parent EXP-INTEL-35422991016 (MEASUREMENT_INVALID): does the OECD/COINr pipeline preserve feature discrimination? A positive result (C3 PASS) unblocks the MIXED program with a specific metric and recipe. A negative result (C3 FAIL) closes the density-based MIXED approach definitively and redirects effort. Either outcome prevents wasted cycles and changes a concrete product decision about MIXED handling strategy.
